overview: Flare Emissions Root-Cause Analytics addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in oil, gas and petrochemicals operations. The first proof of value uses flare flow meters, process alarms and unit events. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is flaring intensity per tonne, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: flare flow meters, process alarms and unit events; define flaring intensity per tonne and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Asset Integrity Director / Production Manager.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for flaring intensity per tonne
